prerequisites: Knowledge of Technical Drawing and Computer-Aided Design (CAD)
Having passed the subjects "Graphic Expression and Assisted Design" (first year) and "Industrial Drawing" (third year)

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to communicate with non-experts in the field.
Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team.
Ability to fluently use IT at a user level.
Knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.

Ability for the drafting, signing, and development of industrial engineering projects whose purpose is the construction, renovation, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their area of study.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Be able to conceptualize and formalize real problems of graphic analysis and synthesis and design.
Be able to use computer resources for the development of virtual models and the generation of drawings.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Introduction to CAD/CAM/CAE. 1.1. CAD Technology (Computer-Aided Design). Processes, tools, and platforms 1.2. CAE Technology. Processes, tools, and platforms 1.3. CAM Technology. Processes, tools, and platforms

Topic 2. Creation and editing techniques on generic and specific CAD tools. 2.1. Creation and editing techniques of geometric entities in generalist CAD systems 2.2. Creation and editing techniques of geometric entities in specialist CAD systems
Topic 3. Design of mechanical elements in 2 dimensions (2D) 3.1. 2D plotting of mechanical engineering elements 3.2. Parametric plotting based on geometric and dimensional constraints
Topic 4. Design of mechanical elements in 2 dimensions (2D) 4.1. 2D plotting of mechanical engineering elements 4.2. Parametric plotting based on geometric and dimensional constraints

Topic 5. Layout of engineering drawings according to harmonized standards. 5.1. Introduction to the development of drawings in industrial engineering 5.2. Indication of dimensions, conventional signs, tolerances, and surface finishes
Topic 6. Design of mechanical assemblies. Relationships between simple elements. 6.1. 3D design of mechanical elements and assemblies. 6.2. Parametric 3D design based on constraints

Topic 7. Organization of graphic documentation in technical office. Typology of drawings. 7.1. Introduction to graphic documentation in engineering project technical offices 7.2. Management of CAD-type files
teaching_methods: Theory classes with practical examples or participative classes
Assessment activities (individual theoretical-practical exam, with practical part on computer)

assessment_methods.method: Participation in theoretical and practical classes
